# automate-apple-shortcuts-automations

Mass-create time-of-day Automations in Apple Shortcuts on macOS — driven by an AI agent, verified end-to-end.
This repo documents the proven pipeline: 288 automations (one per 5-minute slot across 24 hours), created, audited, and deduplicated in one working session.

**Assisted-by: Hermes Agent · GLM 5.3 Flash <hermes-ollamacloud-glm53flash@local>** (generated by `agent-detect trailer assisted-by`)

## What this is

A playbook + design record for using **Hermes Agent** running **GLM 5.3 Flash** (via Ollama Cloud) to automate mass creation of Automations within Apple Shortcuts.
Apple provides no scripting interface for Automations — the GUI is the API — so the agent drives the real UI: keyboard, Accessibility actions, and true mouse events, with machine-verified state after every step.

- **DESIGN.md** — the full design learnings, nifties, and innovations (coordinate spaces, AX vs SwiftUI control behavior, verification loops, OCR tooling, batch orchestration)
- **[scripts/](scripts/README.md)** — the session's working helper scripts, ready to use: generic macOS GUI automation + Shortcuts-app flows (audited against the live app).
  Our own target shortcuts are referenced by name but not included.
- **.plans/** — session plans with verbatim prompt provenance
- This README — how to reproduce it yourself

## What the live run achieved

| | |
|---|---|
| Automations created | 219 (+69 pre-existing = 288 total) |
| Coverage | one per 5-minute slot, 00:00 → 23:55, daily |
| Verification | 288/288 slots, 0 duplicates, 0 gaps, all intervals correct |
| Cleanup | 5 duplicates deleted, 1 wrong-interval automation fixed |
| Machine time | ≈ 70 minutes |

Interval mapping used (change to taste):

- `:00` → **Every Hour**
- `:15`, `:45` → **Every Quarter Hour**
- `:30` → **Every Half Hour**
- all other slots → **Every 5 minutes**

## Requirements

- macOS (developed on macOS 26.x, Apple Silicon)
- Apple Shortcuts (bundled)
- [Hermes Agent](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs) desktop app
- A vision-capable, reciprocity-compliant model in Hermes — the reference setup is **GLM 5.3 Flash via Ollama Cloud** (open-weight model, zero-training cloud provider)
- Local tools the agent will use:
  - `osascript` (bundled) — AppleScript / JXA
  - PyObjC — `uv venv && uv pip install pyobjc-framework-ApplicationServices`
  - optionally a local OCR helper (Swift + Vision framework) — see DESIGN.md §6 for the ~30-line implementation

## How to use it with Hermes + GLM 5.3 Flash

1. **Read the policy first.**
   This project follows [bevry-vibes/skills policy](https://github.com/bevry-vibes/skills/blob/main/policy.md).
   Run `agent-detect check-reciprocal` in your session; it must report reciprocal before proceeding.

2. **Open the target state.** Decide your interval mapping and how far you already are (e.g. "midnight → 5:30am exists").

3. **Prompt Hermes** with something like:

   > I want Automations in Apple Shortcuts for every 5 minutes. I have
   > already done until 5.30am. Hourly automations should run `Every
   > Hour`, every 30 minutes `Every Half Hour`, every 15 minutes `Every
   > Quarter Hour`, and every other 5-minute slot `Every 5 minutes`.
   > All should run immediately. Verify the current state first, then
   > create only what's missing, and give me START/FINISH alerts around
   > every automated run.

4. **Grant permissions when prompted** — Accessibility (System Events + AX reads) and Screen capture. Hermes will tell you what it needs.

5. **Stay hands-off during runs.**
   The agent brackets every automated sequence with visible dialogs.
   When a dialog says START, don't touch mouse or keyboard until FINISH.
   When the agent gets stuck, it hands control back — take over, then hand it back when you're done.

6. **Calibrate interactively when asked.**
   For SwiftUI internals (the time picker, the shortcut card grid) the agent needs one user-parked-mouse calibration per unique control: park your mouse over the element, say "placed", and it reads the exact position and derives the element.
   One calibration covers the whole batch — the dialogs are fixed-size and centered.

7. **Expect an audit pass at the end.**
   The agent reads the full automation list via Accessibility, diffs it against the expected schedule, deletes any duplicates (with your confirmation dialog handled automatically), and re-verifies.
   Ask for the audit report explicitly: *"verify every 5-minute slot exists exactly once with the correct interval"*.

### Prompt patterns that worked

- **Existence-first**: "check what already exists before creating anything" — avoids duplicates from the start.
- **Verify-per-step**: "after every step, verify by reading the accessibility tree / taking a screenshot".
- **Incremental batching**: run the first 5–15, verify, then release the full batch.
- **Named cleanup**: "delete duplicates; the confirm dialog's default button is Cancel, press the red Delete instead".

## What the agent actually does (per automation, ~11–18s)

1. `⌥⌘N` → New Automation → ↓ + Enter → Time of Day sheet
2. True-click the hour field (calibrated point) → type `hh` → → → `mm` → → → `a`/`p`
3. AXPress **Run Immediately**
4. Enter (submits the form) → shortcut picker
5. Click the interval card (calibrated position)
6. Enter (Done) → verify sheet closed, badge incremented

All state changes are verified by AX tree dumps, local OCR, or vision — never assumed.

## Limitations

- **GUI-only**: Apple exposes no scripting for Automations; anything that changes the UI (macOS updates) can shift card positions or sheets.
  The recipes here were proven on macOS 26.x / Shortcuts as of 2026-08.
- **Needs a frontmost, unlocked Mac** during runs (it drives the real UI). Runs are chunked so you can interleave.
- **Timing-sensitive**: ~1% misfire rate at tuned speeds; the audit pass catches and fixes them.
